highlights.title: Meta Pushes Its New AI Agent on Employees—but Eases Off on Tokenmaxxing
highlights.summary: The company is reducing pressure on workers to use artificial intelligence tools while encouraging them to experiment with Hatch, its most advanced AI project yet.
body: Meta is formally ending what amounted to a tokenmaxxing incentive program for employees. In an internal announcement this week, the social media giant told workers that their performance evaluations would no longer be dependent upon how much they used AI tools, three employees who received the message tell WIRED. But as Meta workers simultaneously begin testing a new agentic AI tool known as Hatch, they say their token consumption continues to surge.

New guidance for performance reviews unveiled this week replaces references to evaluating employees based on criteria like “usage of AI” and their “AI Native” designation, with looser wording, which caveats that “these outcomes can be supported by AI or other means.” It restores Meta’s focus to grading employees on their impact, with less regard to how it is achieved. Some Meta employees tell WIRED the changes are subtle but welcome, freeing them from feeling pressured to use AI in situations in which it doesn’t make sense.

highlights.title: From MIT to IBM, expediting AI and quantum deployment
highlights.summary: MIT affiliates engage with the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab to bring rigorous theory to production systems.
body: The experience of transitioning from research based in theory to focusing on real-world application can vary significantly for different researchers. However, for two former MIT graduate students and a former postdoc, all now at IBM, working with the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab (formerly the MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab) during their formative years enabled them to not only close the gap between education and employment, but also to generate ideas promising to business impact.

Despite pursuing varied careers in quantum machine learning, reinforcement learning and artificial intelligence agents,and trustworthy and fair AI, respectively, Srinivasan Arunachalam, Zhang-Wei Hong PhD ’25, and Irene Ko PhD ’24 have consistently found ways to tackle problems defined by novelty and rigor, and translate them to systems with real constraints. Here, the MIT-IBM Computing Research Lab served as a conduit for research relationship building and the flow of their expertise to industry applications.

highlights.title: The 12 Best Star Wars Video Games of All Time, Ranked
highlights.summary: On Aug. 27, Electronic Arts released its newest Star Wars game. Star Wars: Zero Company is one of the best reviewed games ever inspired by the series, offering a compelling blend of tactics and fandom that’s nearly impossible to resist.
body: Star Wars video games date all the way back to The Empire Strikes Back on the Atari 2600 in 1982. Since then, the franchise itself has largely matured alongside the medium. Many of the earliest games are still worth revisiting now, even the ones that were victims of hardware limitations. If you’re wondering where to turn first once you complete Zero Company, here are the 12 best Star Wars games of all time.

Respawn Entertainment has had multiple chances to do Star Wars justice, starting with this first entry in the Star Wars Jedi series. It introduces Cal Kestis, a hero living through the dark period following Revenge of the Sith. Not everyone loves the Jedi, even at the best of times. They feel a bit like the galaxy’s superheroes, and yet there’s no denying the thrill of a good lightsaber duel. Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order focuses on that aspect in particular, and lets players explore interesting environments other games only allow them to glimpse from afar. It’s pretty and fun, despite performance issues at launch and some tedious backtracking.

highlights.title: Jennifer Aniston Joins Boyfriend Jim Curtis For Chat About Health, Wellness and Hypnotherapy
highlights.summary: The couple, who have been dating for over a year, took part in a 92NY event in support of Curtis' new book 'The Book of Possibility.'
body: Jennifer Aniston and Jim Curtis took a very public step in their relationship on Wednesday, sitting down together for a conversation at 92NY.

“Not yet. We’re still on track here. First question please,” Curtis joked back. She began by asking him about his journey to wellness and self-help, after growing up in Boston (where “we didn’t suffer woo-woo,” Curtis said) and having a finance career on Wall Street. Eventually, he hit an “ultimate low” with his health and relationships, and wound up in the hospital with a scary diagnosis.

“I just said, ‘You know what? I’ve reached rock bottom and it’s time to change,'” Curtis told the crowd as he got emotional. Aniston responded, “You reached this point where you’re met with two roads, and you definitely took the road less traveled in your case.”
Curtis has walked with a limp since he was young due to lesions on his spinal cord, and admitted that when people would ask why, he’d say he got into a motorcycle accident.

highlights.title: I used to think I was an ambivalent mother, then my child started to stutter | Bridie Jabour
highlights.summary: I snapped at my children. Resented daily pickup. But I was there when he needed me, and my perception of myself completely changed. I still can’t pinpoint when it happened, but it felt as though my child lost the ability to communicate overnight.
body: Of course, that is not what happened, and he never lost the ability to communicate. But it felt as though he did at the time. And even with the benefit of hindsight, it felt like he went from a chatty three-year-old to being unable to get a sentence out. “W-w-w-w-w-w-w-w-w-what c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-c-can I-I-I-I-I-I-I” and then silence as he gave up trying and just looked up at me.

I often joke my parenting approach is one of benign neglect, and that I lack any instinct at all. I still do lean into that caricature at times (“I will have to do a few minutes of parenting this weekend,” I recently texted the family group chat in mock horror). This joke originated when I first became a mother more than eight years ago. I perpetuated this idea that my children were not the centre of my world and therefore I was somehow different from other mothers.
Privately I thought I was more ambivalent about motherhood than I anticipated. It turns out I had mistaken what maternal ambivalence was.

I still can’t pinpoint when it happened, but it felt as though my child lost the ability to communicate overnight.

highlights.title: Uber beats Waymo as first to launch robotaxis in London
highlights.summary: Uber beat out Waymo in launching a commercial robotaxi service in London, the city's first. The vehicles use autonomous driving tech developed by Wayve, a UK-based startup, and will initially feature safety drivers behind the wheel.
body: The cars have no lidar and no geofence, but still will have human safety drivers for the initial launch.

London-based Uber customers who want to try out these new robot-controlled cars can indicate their preference in the app’s settings. When booking a ride through UberX, Uber Comfort, or Uber Electric, riders may be paired with a Wayve-developed autonomous vehicle, but it’s not a guarantee. Wayve is using Ford Mustang Mach-Es for its fleet, followed by the Nissan Leaf in the future.

Safety drivers will monitor the driving from the front seat, though Uber says they won’t control the driving and will gradually be phased out in favor of fully driverless vehicles. Safety drivers are licensed by Transport for London, the city’s transit authority.

The traditional AV1.0 approach relies on hand-engineered stacks, HD maps and a rule-based approach – this limits scalability and the ability to rapidly generalize to new environments or complex scenarios. Wayve’s AV2.0 takes a different path – a single, learned AI driver trained to understand the world, anticipate risk, and adapt to new environments.

highlights.summary: Google launched Gemini 3.8 Flash, arriving just a few weeks after its predecessor. The company claims the new model "works harder" than Gemini 3.7 Flash by performing more reasoning steps on complex tasks and "calling tools iteratively." It has the same introductory pricing as 3.7 Flash, $0.75 per…
body: Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber is also launching to Google’s new Fairwind Program.

Gemini 3.8 Flash’s launch was followed by some early impressions online. Artificial Analysis highlighted the model’s pricing, saying Gemini 3.8 Flash is “the cheapest we’ve measured at this level of intelligence. This is up ~40% from Gemini 3.7 Flash despite unchanged per-token pricing, driven by a 30% increase in output tokens per task and more turns on agentic evaluations.”

Aigora.ai CEO John Ennis compared Gemini 3.8 Flash to Anthropic’s models, saying it offers “Opus 5 coding quality but at a fraction of the cost and super fast,” adding, “This is going to be so awesome for things like making remotion videos.”

Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash offers “significant improvements” for software engineering and autonomous AI agents. It outperforms its predecessor and other frontier models on the DeepSWE v1.1 software engineering benchmark, including Anthropic’s Fable 5, which got an upgrade earlier this week that also promises stronger performance at a lower price, by cutting the price to use cached data.

LG's C-series OLED TV in general has been our favorite TVs for console gaming for many years thanks to its outstanding image quality, low input lag, and high refresh rate. This is one of the best TVs you can get for streaming 4K HDR content in its intended glory. It boasts the near-infinite black levels, near-infinite contrast ratio, and near-instantaneous response times you'd expect from any OLED TV. It's also equipped with LG's proprietary Evo panel, which is significantly brighter and offers a wider color gamut than traditional W-OLED TVs.

The C6 is also equipped with modern gaming features that make it a perfect complement to current generation consoles like the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, including a native 120Hz panel that can be pushed to as high as 165Hz, HDMI 2.1 inputs, variable refresh rate and auto low latency mode.

highlights.title: Spending deal comes with a bonus: Blocking political control of grants
highlights.summary: On Tuesday, the House of Representatives passed a stopgap measure that would continue funding the US government through early December. While the measure still requires the signature of President Trump, it's widely expected that he will act to avoid a government shutdown immediately before the…
body: This is a normal part of how the US government has operated in recent years, as it's often difficult to build the political support needed to pass a full year's budget in advance. In fact, dissent within the House's Republican caucus prevented them from agreeing on their own measure to keep the government open; instead, the House simply adopted a version of the spending bill that had previously passed the Senate.

From the perspective of scientists and their supporters, that adoption turned out to be a very good thing. Because the Senate's budget bill, passed in early August, contains a provision that blocks the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) from implementing new rules that would give political appointees full control over what science is funded and allow them to cancel any grant at any time. The proposed rule has been widely decried as catastrophic for science, and it faced widespread opposition from scientific and health-focused organizations.

highlights.title: Trump Administration Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Lawsuit
highlights.summary: The US government wrote a letter in support of OpenAI’s argument that training AI on others' intellectual property is fair use.
body: The Trump Administration just took OpenAI’s side in the artificial intelligence company’s legal battle with the New York Times.

The media juggernaut sued OpenAI and Microsoft in 2023, alleging that the companies had violated copyright law by training their AI tools on its articles without permission. Now, the government has stepped in, arguing that OpenAI’s actions were within bounds.

The letter argued that the Times’ definition of fair use is “inconsistent” with current copyright law, and that a win for the paper could have disastrous consequences. “Constraining LLM development under a misunderstanding of fair use doctrine would thwart such creative and scientific progress while hindering American prosperity and economic mobility,” lawyers for the government wrote.
While the letter focuses on the New York Times and OpenAI, the government noted that its arguments apply to all of the parties in this case and related cases, including other publishers and authors.

highlights.summary: Sequelizing 2022’s surprise horror-thriller hit Fall could be a simple assignment: Find a bunch of other victims and dangle them from the top of another tower. But like the foolhardy heroes at the center of this week’s Fall 2: Deadpoint, directors Michael and Peter Spierig weren’t looking for a…
body: “We didn't wanna make it a tower or anything similar to the first film,” Peter Spierig tells Polygon. “There was just no point of going there again.”

For the brothers, Fall writer-director Scott Mann set the bar — ahem — high. So, instead of chasing that glory again, they looked at real-world environments that could offer both a visceral thrill more room for character movement and varying set pieces. The solution: recreate China’s Huashan Plank Walk, which by all accounts is… a legit IRL nightmare.

Thousands of people attempt versions of the real-world attraction each year, and videos of it gave the filmmakers a useful preview of exactly what audiences would find terrifying. Their characters could go up and down and left and right.
“We could go sideways and have all kinds of bad things happen,” Peter says.

highlights.title: Samsung's Frame Pro isn't just a gorgeous TV, it opened my eyes to art
highlights.summary: The design-forward TV delivers a performance that few in the category can – while attracting compliments as wall decor. Can’t hear what’s playing on TV? It’s not your ears, it’s the flat screen. These affordable soundbars can help.
body: When they are screening blockbusters, huge TVs are cinematic portals to another world. When they’re off, huge TVs are hideous black mirrors. Samsung has always understood this home decor landmine and aimed to defuse it in 2017 with The Frame, the first-ever “art TV”: a television disguised as a framed painting.

As a female tech editor who spent years appraising the banal designs of 1990s tech, I can palpably remember how thrilled I was to see this innovative melding of form and function, which seemed like a novel luxury at the time. Fast-forward nearly a decade, and Samsung’s pricey niche concept has gone decisively mainstream, with competition from LG, Hisense, TCL and even Amazon.
But Samsung hasn’t been sitting still: The Frame Pro boasts cordless architecture, a matte screen and customizable magnetic bezels.

highlights.title: These Russian Mathematicians Taught AI Models How to Talk to Each Other Without Using Words
highlights.summary: A startup called Mostik has a wild new approach to combining the capabilities of AI models.
body: I recently met with some brilliant Russian mathematicians who showed me a way for artificial intelligence models to communicate via something akin to machine telepathy.

The mathematicians work for a startup called Mostik—the Russian word for bridge. It’s a nod to the group’s approach, which allows different models to interact using the mathematical values found in their weights —the things that determine how a prompt gets turned into an output. In practice, this means the capabilities of a larger model can be fed to a smaller model to ramp up its intelligence much more efficiently.

The startup used the approach to build a model that has rocketed to the top of ARC-AGI 3, a notoriously difficult competition for AI models. (They wouldn’t tell me more because they want to win the contest.) To demonstrate the idea, however, they also created a bridge between two Chinese open-weight models: the largest version of GLM-5.2, which has 753 billion parameters; and a 4-billion-parameter version of Qwen-3.5 that can run on a mobile device. The resulting hybrid system costs one-twentieth of the full GLM model, and its performance is exactly halfway between the two.
points: A startup called Mostik has a wild new approach to combining the capabilities of AI models.

body: Alexa for Shopping can compare the message you received ‘against a record of every message Amazon has sent.’

As noted by Amazon, the assistant will only confirm that a message is real if it’s “completely certain.” An example shared by Amazon shows a customer asking, “Did Amazon just text me an OTP from 98626? Message came around 4:50pm.” Alexa for Shopping responds by confirming that Amazon actually did send the message, saying, “This was a genuine One Time Password from Amazon.”

If Alexa for Shopping determines a message isn’t from Amazon, it will instruct customers to check their orders in the app and contact Amazon’s support team directly. The company launched a similar feature earlier this year that lets you forward suspicious messages to “verify@amazon.com” to check if they’re real.
This isn’t the only recent update Amazon has launched for Alexa for Shopping, as it added an “Update Me When” feature that can now help you track new product releases as well.

highlights.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
highlights.summary: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).
body: The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.

body: It’s entirely possible we’re not seeing Sea of Sorrows anytime soon. Longtime fans may remember Silksong itself was originally planned as DLC for Hollow Knight, before growing into a massive, standalone sequel. So, whether you’re waiting a few months or seven years, you could probably use another game or two to pass the time. We’ve rounded up seven games, across genres, that Silksong fans are sure to love.

Zelda 2: The Adventure of Link, alongside Metroid, Faxanandu, and Mega Man, was one of several NES titles that inspired Hollow Knight. Of every game in The Legend of Zelda’s 40-year history, it makes sense that Zelda 2 heavily influenced Team Cherry. For one, it’s unlike any other Zelda game. It’s a side-scroller with RPG elements, reminiscent of some Castlevania titles. It’s also the hardest Zelda game by a long shot. Enemies are fast, lives are limited, and, if you die, you’re sent all the way back to the beginning of the game. Talk about a runback.

highlights.title: How Doll Invasion Went From a Trans House Party to a Fire Island Mainstay
highlights.summary: "It was transsexual summer camp," Doll Invasion founder Fran Tirado recalls of the now-annual Fire Island celebration and fundraiser's humble beginnings.
body: About a decade ago, I took my maiden voyage to the 31-mile stretch of sand along the southern shore of New York known as Fire Island. At the time, I didn’t know that much about the Pines. I’d heard about “tea” and the whole concept as a kind of gay guy Treasure Island for brave New Yorkers who took a train to another train, then a shuttle, then a ferry in search of known and unknown plunder.
Later, when I found myself at a RuGirl-studded pool party co-sponsored by a vodka brand and a gay dating app, I realized that people did, in fact, know this place. Just not my people.

Year after year, I’d return to the island to reprise that tradition. Then I started pitching around the concept of a “Doll Invasion.” I wanted to rent a house, book some DJs, and throw an actual party, inviting trans people—and anyone who loved trans people—to overcome the deterrent of the island’s reputation and make their own maiden voyages.
